subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the registration-mode bug is fixed, should OpenClaw accept this official external MXC sandbox plugin with `@microsoft/mxc-sdk`/`node-pty` native binaries and the SDK's argv-carried base64 config transport?
rationale: Automation can repair the missing registration guard, but it cannot approve a new native sandbox dependency graph or decide whether the preview SDK argv transport is acceptable for an official sandbox backend.

options.title: Fix guard, then approve exact head
options.body: Repair the non-full registration side effect and then let maintainer/secops approve the final dependency graph and documented preview SDK boundary.

options.title: Pause for upstream transport
options.body: Hold this PR until MXC provides a non-argv config transport, reducing process-visibility concerns before OpenClaw ships the plugin.

options.title: Move out of first-party review
options.body: Decline first-party packaging for now and ask for a community/ClawHub-only plugin until the native dependency boundary matures.

recommendation.title: Fix guard, then approve exact head
recommendation.body: Repair the non-full registration side effect and then let maintainer/secops approve the final dependency graph and documented preview SDK boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned on the live PR and has relevant history around OpenShell sandbox/plugin registration behavior.
